plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid, not your own bid—so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. With a private value of $9, I will bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding truthfully (equal to my private value) is the dominant strategy. Since I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot round, the optimal approach is to bid exactly my value of $40, ensuring I maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategy-proof. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - I cannot benefit from bidding higher or lower than my actual value of $32. If I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying relative to my value. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
